title: SC PSC Order No. 2026-152H — Standing Hearing Officer Directive Order Accepting Power Purchase Agreement and Granting Request for Confidential Treatment - Power Purchase Agreement Between Duke Energy Progress, LLC and Stripe Solar, LLC
summary: Standing Hearing Officer Directive Order Accepting Power Purchase Agreement and Granting Request for Confidential Treatment - Power Purchase Agreement Between Duke Energy Progress, LLC and Stripe Solar, LLC
text:
PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION OF SOUTH CAROLINA 

STANDING HEARING OFFICER DIRECTIVE 

DOCKET NO. 2026-160-E ORDER NO. 2026-152-H 

JULY 7, 2026 

STANDING HEARING OFFICER: C. Jo Anne Wessinger Hill, Esquire 

DOCKET DESCRIPTION: DOCKET NO. 2026-160-E – Power Purchase Agreement Between 
Duke Energy Progress, LLC and Stripe Solar, LLC 

MATTER UNDER CONSIDERATION: Request by Duke Energy Progress, LLC (DEP) for 
the Commission to grant Confidential Treatment to the Power Purchase Agreement (“PPA” or 
“Agreement”) between Duke Energy Progress, LLC (DEP) and Stripe Solar, LLC (Stripe Solar) 
filed on June 24, 2026 (DEP Letter/Request). 

HEARING OFFICER’S ACTION: This matter comes before the Hearing Officer on a Request 
by DEP pursuant to S.C. Code Ann. section 58-41-20(E)(1), S.C. Code Ann. Regs. 103-804 and 
Commission Order No. 2005-226, as amended by Orders No. 2020-490 and 2023-859, seeking 
Confidential Treatment of certain portions of the Power Purchase Agreement between DEP and 
Stripe Solar. Section 58-41-20(E)(1) mandates that all electric “utilities shall file with the 
commission power purchase agreements entered into pursuant to PURPA, resulting from 
voluntary negotiation of contracts between an electrical utility and a small power producer not 
eligible for the standard offer.” S.C. Code Ann. § 58-41-20(E)(1) (Supp. 2025) (emphasis added). 

In submitting the filing, DEP asserts that “[d]ue to the commercial sensitivity and proprietary 
nature of certain portions of the Agreement, DEP respectfully requests that the Commission find 
that, pursuant to S.C. Code Ann. Regs. 103-804(S)(2) and S.C. Code Ann. § 30-4-40(a)(1), certain 
provisions of the Agreement are exempt from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act, 
S.C. Code Ann. §§ 30-4-10 et seq.” DEP Letter/Request, p. 1. DEP further asserts that 
confidentiality is sought for identified confidential information and relevant provisions of the 
Agreement for which DEP “derives economic value” from such information “not being generally 
known to, and not being readily ascertainable by proper means, by other persons who would be 
able to obtain economic value from its disclosure.” Id. Additionally, DEP states that the redacted 
and confidential provisions are “confidential pricing and conditions, as well as delivery parameters 
and details of the operating characteristics of the facility, all of which are proprietary and specific 
to this counter-party [Stripe Solar].” Id. DEP further states that the specific redactions and 
confidentiality in the Agreement were mutually reviewed and agreed upon by both DEP and Stripe 
Solar, as well as the parties agreeing not to disclose any term of these confidential provisions to a 
third party without the prior written consent of the other party. Id. 

Commission Regulation 103-804(S)(2) provides that the Commission, within its discretion, can 
determine what matters are placed and available in the public record on the DMS. S.C. Code Ann. 
Regs. 103-804(S)(2) (2012). Likewise, the Commission has discretion to determine what matters 
are exempt from public disclosure, including exemption from release under the Freedom of 
Information Act, S.C. Code Ann. §§ 30-4-10 et seq. Id. 

STANDING HEARING OFFICER DIRECTIVE NO. 2026-152-H 
DOCKET NOS. 2026-160-E 
JULY 7, 2026 
PAGE 2 OF 2 

In support of the Request and in protection of this information, DEP complied with the 
requirements of Commission Order 2005-226, as amended by Orders No. 2020-490 and 2023-859. 
Additionally, DEP provided a confidential version and a redacted public version of the Agreement 
to the Commission and the Office of Regulatory Staff. There were no objections to the Request 
for Confidential Treatment requested by DEP. 

Considering the Request of DEP and acts in compliance with Orders No. 2005-226, 2020-490, and 
2023-859, the Hearing Officer finds that confidential treatment of the Power Purchase 
Agreement between Duke Energy Progress, LLC, and Stripe Solar, LLC, is warranted. 
Accordingly, the Request for Confidential Treatment filed by Duke Energy Progress, LLC, 
is granted as requested. The Power Purchase Agreement between Duke Energy Progress, LLC, 
and Stripe Solar, LLC, is exempt from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act, S.C. 
Code Ann. §§ 30-4-10 et seq. The Commission shall maintain the confidential version of this 
Agreement as confidential unless or until the Commission rules such information is not entitled to 
protection from public disclosure, or Duke Energy Progress, LLC, and Stripe Solar, LLC, agree 
that such information is no longer confidential, commercially sensitive, or proprietary. 

The Hearing Officer further accepts for filing the Power Purchase Agreement between Duke 
Energy Progress, LLC, and Stripe Solar, LLC, on behalf of the Commission. 

This concludes the Hearing Officer’s Directive.
